text:
Maria S.: Heads up — OSS scan flagged CVE-2026-0458 in libwebsockets. PoC seen on a forked repo but exploitability is unclear. This touches websocket-gateway used by streaming and realtime APIs. Need a decision: emergency hotfix vs scheduled patch window. SLA/customer tier implications?

Kevin L.: Can you paste the triage summary? Which versions hit, and which services? Also call out whether Dedicated customers are affected (they might be pinned).

Ash K.: Triage summary: libwebsockets vuln in handshake parser -> memory corruption (RCE risk). Affects <4.2.0. PoC exists but requires specific handshake framings; we have small exposure on websocket-gateway (prod) and analytics-replay (internal). Dedicated nodes pinned to 4.1.8 are impacted. Proposed plan: backport security fix into our websocket-proxy adapter, run 2h canary in staging, then staged rollout to hosted.

Maria S.: If we do a rolling restart for the gateway, what's the latency/SLA hit? Any chance of dropped connections / data loss for streaming customers?

Kevin L.: Rolling restart will restart pods one at a time. Each pod takes ~45s to drain + ~30s to start healthy. We'll see short connection reconnections for persistent websocket clients; most SDKs auto-reconnect. No data loss (we don't keep in-flight state). Latency blips for ~2-3% of requests during rollout if concurrency skewed. For enterprise customers on Dedicated, we should coordinate maintenance windows.

Lina Q.: From a compliance angle: ensure audit logs show the patch rollout and any KMS key accesses. If config changes touch key identifiers, we must not rotate key material mid-rollout. Also add RBAC checks for the deploy role so only ops+sec can trigger the emergency path.

Ash K.: Risk gating proposal: severity = high, exploitability = limited -> P1 for hosted (must patch within 24h), P2 for Dedicated unless customer requests immediate action. Timeline suggestion:
- PR with backport today (owner: @ash)
- Canary in staging after PR merge (2h) 
- 12h canary with traffic shaping (prod-read replicas)
- Full staged rollout over 24-36h depending on telemetry

Kevin L.: Agree but add cohorting: S1 = PLG/free (auto-patch), S2 = paid (auto-patch w/ notification), S3 = enterprise (contact account owners + schedule within their maintenance window, offer opt-in for immediate hotfix). We should also prepare an SLA credit FAQ in case customers call it out.

Maria S.: Backout plan? If the patch causes regressions we need a safe revert path and a toggle to disable new behavior quickly.

Ash K.: Backout details:
```
# Rollback deploy
kubectl rollout undo deployment/websocket-gateway --namespace=prod
# If quick toggle needed
kubectl patch configmap/websocket-config -n prod -p '{"data":{"wslib_security_fix":"off"}}'
```
We tested rollback in staging. Also keep the previous image in the registry for instant revert.

Lina Q.: I added audit checklist to the incident tracker: ensure entries for:
- who initiated the deploy
- KMS key id used for any connection tokens updated
- RBAC approver name
Please tag me before merge: @lina. Also ensure our KMS client library is not being upgraded to a breaking minor during this change.

deploy-bot: :rocket: canary rollout started for websocket-gateway (canary=2 pods) — monitor pods/websocket-gateway-canary

oncall-bot: Incident note created: ENGSEC-2026-0427 (libwebsockets triage). Owner assigned: @ash.

Kevin L.: I'll coordinate comms with Sales for S3 customers. @maria, can you draft a short customer-facing blurb for status page? Keep it factual: we patched a third-party lib with potential exploit, scheduled restarts may cause brief reconnects, no evidence of customer data exfiltration.

Maria S.: Will do. Draft ready in ~1h and will post to status.redwood.ai once we hit production canary metrics.

Ash K.: Locking PR and starting canary. Will ping when metrics look clean or if we hit elevated error rates (>0.5% 5xx).

Lina Q.: I'll watch audit logs and KMS logs, and confirm no unexpected key fetches.

Maria S.: Thanks team. Decision: emergency patch path with staged rollout + cohorted customer notifications. Owners: @ash (patch), @kevin (customer comms), @lina (audit/RBAC), @maria (status page).
